Introduction

We will show you several choice activities about possible responses in a future pandemic. These scenarios are described in terms of:

  • The type of public health measures in place and how long they last

  • The expected impacts on:

    1. Health (cases/deaths)

    2. Education

    3. The economy

  • Whether a vaccine is available by the end of the measures

The public health measures and duration

To reduce infections and deaths before a vaccine is available, the government may introduce different packages of public health measures (for example, social distancing or a lockdown).

In the options you will be shown, these measures may be in place intermittently over a period of 3, 6, or 9 months. This means restrictions may be introduced, eased, and reintroduced during that time.

3 months 6 months 9 months

Public health measures

Type of restrictions Description
Basic measures
  • Encouraging hand washing, cleaning and disinfection, and opening windows in shared spaces
  • Contact tracing and isolation for people who are infected.
  • Some border measures (for example, screening or quarantine).
  • Face masks recommended in public.
  • Shielding for clinically extremely vulnerable groups
Reduced social contact

  • Physical distancing in public places.

  • Only small groups from different households can meet.

  • Restrictions on public gatherings and events.

  • Large events such as concerts and sports matches are cancelled.
Lockdown
  • Stay-at-home order in place.
  • Schools and early years settings are closed.
  • Most workplaces are closed except essential services.
  • All public events and gatherings cancelled.

Health impacts

The number of deaths caused by the pandemic over one year, either because of the disease itself or from wider impacts of the pandemic (e.g., access to routine care).

Low Mid High

The chance that you or someone in your household will catch the disease over one year

25% infection risk 50% infection risk 90% infection risk

Wider impacts on society

Economic impacts: A pandemic and the measures used to contain it can affect the economy, resulting in business closures. In this survey, economic impact is shown as the number of local businesses (such as shops, cafés, restaurants, and other services) in your area that close over the next 12 months because of the pandemic, and do not reopen after restrictions are lifted.

No impact 1 in 5 close 2 in 5 close

Educational impacts: A pandemic can affect children’s learning through school closures, missed lessons, stress and anxiety, and lower attendance. In this survey, this is shown as the number of extra children in a class of 25 who remain behind in their learning for at least five years because of the pandemic.

5 in 25 fall behind 10 in 25 fall behind

Vaccines

Vaccines can now be developed more quickly than in the past. In each scenario, you will be told whether a vaccine is expected to be available when the public health measures end.

If a vaccine becomes available, it may help society return to normal more quickly by providing another way to protect people from the disease.

You should assume the vaccine would be:

  • Approved by the NHS as safe and effective. This means: 
    • Common side effects are mild and serious side effects are very rare 
    • The vaccine greatly reduces the risk of severe illness and death 
  • Free of out-of-pocket charge
  • Available to everyone, but rolled out in phases  

You would not be required to get the vaccine, but it is strongly recommended to help protect yourself and others.
